lesson: Never embed agent self-references in user-facing output. Forbidden phrases: 'FQC-ARR', 'Finance ARR Quarter Close', 'supervisor', 'sub-agent', 'autonomous agent', 'auto-generated by ...', 'Authored by ...', or any trailing signature/footer block in Jira comments, Slack messages, PR bodies, or generated files. Lead with the ticket key and the substance. Enforced by .cursor/rules/no-agent-signatures.mdc.
evidence: User explicitly asked to strip the 'Posted by FQC-ARR debugger' footer from a Jira RCA comment and then promoted it to a global rule.

lesson: `slk search` against the enterprise Slack workspace hangs reliably after a small number of queries. Cap to one search per session, prefer cached user ids in data/slack_directory.json, and kill any running `slk` PID before retrying.
evidence: Multiple `slk search` calls for <person> and <person>'s user ids hung indefinitely in the EDAEM-3772 session.

lesson: Snowflake MCP `snowflake_query` accepts exactly ONE statement per call. Inline any `SET` constants into the WHERE clause instead of stacking `SET ...; SET ...; SELECT ...`.
evidence: Validation query for EDAEM-3772 returned 'Actual statement count 3 did not match the desired statement count 1' until consolidated.

lesson: Architecture follows the multi-agent Supervisor / Manager pattern (OpenAI 'Practical Guide to Building Agents' 2025; LangGraph; Anthropic 'Building Effective Agents' Dec 2024). The Supervisor holds state and dispatches; sub-agents are stateless workers. Never let a sub-agent talk to another sub-agent directly - go through the supervisor.

Public identity is FQC-ARR (Finance ARR Quarter Close). All aliases - FQC, FQCARR, FQC-ARR, 'Finance ARR Quarter Close', 'ARR Quarter Close', 'ARR close' - resolve to the same supervisor. Never rename the folder, module, class, or rule filenames - it would break every import / rule glob / data-agent reference.

Every sub-agent returns a typed RoleResult (role, status in {ok, needs_input, warn, fail, skipped}, summary, payload, artifacts, pause_reason, preferred_model). The supervisor ONLY reads typed fields - never parse free-form text out of summary. Add new fields to the contract, don't smuggle them through summary.

All public dataclasses must be JSON-serializable via asdict() - no Path / datetime / Enum in the public field set. Convert to string at the boundary. This keeps SDK / SANA / pytest mock callers portable.

Snowflake / Salesforce / dbt / Sigma queries always go through MCP via CallMcpTool - never write Python scripts that authenticate directly (externalbrowser SSO hangs the agent for minutes). Jira and Confluence are the explicit exception: use curl + API token from $JIRA_EMAIL / $JIRA_API_TOKEN. Google Drive has no MCP - use Snowflake's BASE_PROD.GOOGLE_SHEETS.* if Fivetran-synced, else CSV export URL, manual download, or cursor-ide-browser MCP.

Use ref()/source() exclusively in dbt models - never hardcode table names. Use `{{ tcv_to_arr() }}` / `{{ tcv_to_acv() }}` macros (TCV is raw from Agreement Line; ARR annualizes over contract term; ACV normalizes to first-year). Corrected TCV is always COALESCE(corrected_tcv, raw_tcv) via stg_em_lkp_wd_fin_tcv_correction.

Default LLM model = claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh. Override precedence: --model > $FQC_ARR_DEFAULT_MODEL > contracts.DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL. The supervisor itself runs NO LLM. Only requirements_analyzer / clarifier / implementer (+ debugger fix prompt) are LLM-driven; they emit `preferred_model` on the RoleResult so the caller (Cursor SDK, SANA, Cursor chat) routes to the right model.

Three auth modes: FULL_AUTO (no pauses, only when explicitly authorized), SMART_GATES (default - pauses before Jira/PR/Slack/QA writes), GATED_MINIMAL, GATED_FULL. CLI `--auto` is the shortcut for FULL_AUTO. NEVER push to GitHub or open a PR in any mode except FULL_AUTO without an explicit approval pause - the pr-author enforces this hard rule.

ARRCloseOrchestrator accepts a `runner` callable (argv, cwd) -> CompletedProcess. Substituting the runner is the entire portability story: Local CLI uses default_runner (subprocess), Cursor SDK wraps a dbt MCP call, dbt Cloud / SANA wraps POST /jobs/.../run/, tests pass a lambda returning canned CompletedProcess. Never bypass this seam.

Validate at the finest grain (account_id, agreement_id, fiscal_quarter_name, arr_category, product_code_l3, as_was_date). Fixed test agreement_ids that have surfaced refactor bugs before: a1X4X000007UyvvUAC, a1X80000001uPYwEAM, a1XVT00000CSn6w2AD.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing thread: 5+ RCA rounds against PVQ for ssr_off_cycle, up_for_renewal, sku_change_list mismatches.

lesson: PVQ vs QA divergence is NOT automatically a refactor bug. Three buckets: (1) Intentional design change (e.g. `is_ssr.last_fq_for_agreement` replacing `term_end_in_quarter` - PVQ design decision, NOT a regression). (2) Sourcing change with same logical intent (e.g. `finance_line_data` via `finance_line_analytics` join instead of `bt_sku_analytics` - may yield different values when joins behave differently). (3) True refactor regression (must be fixed). Classify category BEFORE proposing a fix.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - `is_ssr` change was bucket (1); `up_for_renewal_fn` dual term_end fan-out was bucket (3).

lesson: Refactor RCA reports follow a stable filename convention: `${HOME}/Documents/Cursor/Documents/Refactor_QA/pvq_qa_rca_report_<YYYY-MM-DD>.html`. Always cite the report path + issue number when posting an RCA back to Jira (e.g. 'issue-1 for as_was_date 2026-04-12'); never restate the analysis from memory.

lesson: `finance_line_analytics` history depth differs sharply by DB: CERTIFIED_DEV holds only the last ~7 as_was_dates, while CERTIFIED_PROD holds the full 70+ day history. Any function or model that `ref()`s finance_line_analytics will pull a SHORT window when deployed in dev, producing apparent gaps vs prod. Always run historical recon queries against CERTIFIED_QA or CERTIFIED_PROD - never CERTIFIED_DEV.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - root-cause table showed dev had 7 distinct as_was_dates, prod had 71.

lesson: Multi-repo awareness: ARR work spans THREE repos that move in lockstep during IA Refactor: eda-dbt-base (sources, SCD2) -> eda-dbt-gtm (staging wrappers) -> eda-dbt-em (finance models). Plus eda-dbt-semantic-layer is a SEPARATE repo for downstream metric definitions. A refactor PR in eda-dbt-em may need a parallel PR in semantic-layer (or the metric definitions break). Always grep across all four repos before declaring scope done.
evidence: Refactoring Code Fixes thread: PR review of eda-dbt-semantic-layer #51 alongside eda-dbt-em #339.

lesson: Snowflake databases for the ED&A finance stack are BASE_PROD (raw), FINANCE_INT_PROD (intermediate / staging), FINANCE_PROD (published managed + aggregates + dashboards), and SALES_PROD (eda-dbt-gtm published). All are Terraform-managed under ROLE_SYSTEM_ADMIN_PROD. Note the actual name is FINANCE_INT_PROD (NOT finance_prod_int).

FINANCE_PROD has three primary schemas: MANAGED (SCD1/SCD2 dimensions: wd_agreement, wd_agreement_scd2, wd_agreement_line_scd2, finance_line_analytics), AGGREGATIONS (arr_line_categories, arr_product_categories, arr_sku_categories, arr_subproduct_categories, arr_account_product_corp_report), DATA_PRODUCTS (the dashboard views).
FINANCE_INT_PROD has a single STAGE schema holding every stg_em_* and stg_arr_categories_* intermediate. When debugging upstream of an aggregate, always look at FINANCE_INT_PROD.STAGE first.

SALES_PROD.MANAGED is the eda-dbt-gtm published layer: wd_account, wd_account_scd2, wd_proposal, wd_proposal_line, wd_proposal_line_scd2, wd_opportunity_daily_snapshot. Cross-project refs from eda-dbt-em consume these via {{ ref('eda_dbt_gtm', 'wd_account_scd2') }}.

Heavy ARR tables (sizes 2026-06-24): ARR_LINE_CATEGORIES = 1.3B rows / 724 GB, ARR_SKU_CATEGORIES = 697M / 86 GB, ARR_SUBPRODUCT_CATEGORIES = 598M / 74 GB, ARR_PRODUCT_CATEGORIES = 588M / 73 GB, ARR_ACCOUNT_PRODUCT_CORP_REPORT = 431M / 98 GB, FINANCE_LINE_ANALYTICS = 355M / 95 GB. Always WHERE as_was_date = <one date> before joining or scanning, otherwise queries cost a lot.

Daily prod refresh window for ARR aggregates is 02:00-03:30 PT: FINANCE_LINE_ANALYTICS finishes ~02:13, ARR_LINE_CATEGORIES ~03:05, then ARR_PRODUCT/SUBPRODUCT/SKU_CATEGORIES 03:24-03:27, ARR_ACCOUNT_PRODUCT_CORP_REPORT ~03:41. Dashboard views are stateless and refresh after their source tables. WD_AGREEMENT_* MANAGED tables refresh in the evening (~22:00 PT) on a separate job.

There are 7 ARR data-product views in models/finance/modeled/data_product/view/: arr_product_customer_retention_dashboard, arr_product_customer_retention_incrementals_dashboard, arr_product_net_dollar_retention_dash, arr_product_relativeattach_dashboard, arr_sku_aggregate, arr_sku_analytics_dashboard, arr_sku_trends_dashboard. All published to FINANCE_PROD.DATA_PRODUCTS.

Deployment gap: arr_product_net_dollar_retention_dash exists in qa code under models/finance/modeled/data_product/view/ but the Snowflake VIEW object is NOT yet present in FINANCE_PROD.DATA_PRODUCTS as of 2026-06-25. Either pending first deploy or deployed under a different name. Check before referencing this view in stakeholder deliverables.

End-to-end ARR DAG: BASE_PROD.SALESFORCE.* (raw) -> eda_dbt_base SCD2 wrappers -> eda_dbt_gtm wd_*_scd2 -> eda_dbt_em stg_em_int_agree_base / stg_em_int_financial_metrics -> stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag (the fan-in) -> finance_line_analytics (currency-converted, published in MANAGED) -> get_arr_line_base_fn (Snowflake function) + stg_arr_categories_* -> arr_line_categories -> arr_product/subproduct/sku_categories -> data_product views.

arr_line_categories grain = one row per (line_id, as_was_date, fiscal_quarter_name). line_id is built by {{ build_line_id() }} macro. Term spans multiple fiscal quarters -> get_fiscal_quarter_fn explodes to one row per FQ. Always filter on as_was_date when querying.

arr_product_categories grain = one row per (as_was_date, account_id, agreement_id, opportunity_id, product_code_l3, fiscal_quarter_name, arr_category). Documented at top of file. Rolls up arr_line_categories from line grain to product (l3) grain.

finance_line_analytics grain = one row per agreement_line_item per as_was_date (incremental filter `where as_was_date = {{ var('as_was_date') }}`). Acquisition flag dedup uses QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by agreement_line_item_key ordered by entity_source nulls last.

Canonical ARR category values from get_arr_categories_fn: 'Net New', 'Add On', 'Expansion', 'Contraction', 'SKU Churn', 'Subproduct Churn', 'Product Churn', 'Logo Churn', 'not categorized'. These appear in three columns per row: sku_arr_category (l5), subproduct_arr_category (l4), product_arr_category (l3).

ARR begin_category triggers: 'Net New' when account_begin_balance = 0 AND it's the first opp on the account this FQ. 'Add On' when account has prior balance but THIS sku had 0 begin balance AND was not in the prior product_mix. Both require term_end >= fiscal_quarter_end_date (line still active at FQ end).

ARR end_category triggers: 'Logo Churn' when account_end_balance = 0 AND end_mix is empty AT FQ END (term_end < current_date). 'SKU Churn' when this sku is not in end_sku_mix AND end_sku_arr = 0 AND sku_churn_fq_end_date = fiscal_quarter_end_date.

Standalone -> Buy Core conversion (get_arr_categories_fn lines 322-480): if begin_sku_category = 'Add On' AND account previously had only peripheral products (Peakon, Strategic Sourcing, PLNF, VNDLY, PLNFC, HiredScore Recruiting/Talent Management, Evisort, Paradox variants, Conversational ATS, Sana/Workday Sana) AND adds HCM or FIN, the line is reclassified to 'Net New' (NOT Add On). Three identical case statements for sku/subproduct/product tiers.

Single-opp special case in get_arr_categories_fn: when opp_count = 1 for a (account_id, agreement_id, product_code_l5, FQ) AND split_arr = 0, the SKU-level balance drives Expansion/Contraction (no other opp to offset against). Without this rule, single-opp lines with intra-line price/quantity restructuring would mis-classify.

Hardcoded override in arr_line_categories.sql L198-236: agreement_id 'a1X4X00000GAh8NUAT' has special ARR category remapping. FY24-Q3..FY25-Q3 'Expansion' -> 'Add On'. FY25-Q4 'Contraction' or 'Expansion' -> 'Product Churn'. Applies at sku, subproduct, and product tiers. Known anti-pattern: hardcoded agreement_id in model.

Three USD currency variants flow through finance_line_analytics: USD_CURRENT (constant_currency_table function, latest rate), USD_HIST (historical_currency_table function, rate at transaction date), USD_ACTUAL (actual_currency_table function, no conversion). All three computed for every monetary column via get_currency_converted_columns(convert_column_array) macro.

Currency join semantics in finance_line_analytics: agreement-context monetary columns (TCV, ARR) use COALESCE(agreement_currency_iso_code, 'USD') matched against term_start. Opportunity-context monetary columns (ACV, opp_*) use COALESCE(opp_currencyisocode, 'USD') matched against close_date. Never use a single currency context for both.

Currency tables are Snowflake FUNCTIONS, not dbt models: select * from table({{ generate_function_db_schema_name() }}.constant_currency_table()) (or historical_currency_table / actual_currency_table). The generate_function_db_schema_name macro resolves the schema name dynamically based on dbt_project.yml vars custom_function_database + custom_function_schema (default: FINANCE.MANAGED).

SSR (Supersede & Replace) detection lives in ssr_process_fn (Snowflake function). Returns 'New', 'Old', or 'Not SSR'. Two sources unioned: (a) Google-sheet ref via {{ ref('eda_dbt_base', 'base_google_sheets_ref_wd_ssr_mapping_ref_wd_ssr_mapping') }} (manual SSR list), (b) BASE_PROD.UNIFIED_HISTORY_RELATED_AGREEMENT_SCD2 filtered to apttus__relationship_to_type__c = 'Is Supersede For'.

SSR PIT (point-in-time) semantics: the SCD2 lookup uses convert_timezone('America/Los_Angeles', 'UTC', to_timestamp(concat(ssr_as_was_date, ' 23:59:59'))) BETWEEN dbt_valid_from AND dbt_valid_to. Always end-of-PT-day. Dedup with QUALIFY MAX(systemmodstamp) OVER (PARTITION BY apttus__apts_contract_to__c).

SSR business rule: SSR transitions are continuity, NOT churn-then-new. ARR category for SSR lines must resolve to FLAT_RENEWAL / EXPANSION / CONTRACTION, never 'Logo Churn' + 'Net New'. The downstream ssr_agreement_relationship + arr_categories logic handles this; do not double-count by treating Old and New agreements independently.

3-tier override mechanism in arr_line_categories + finance_line_analytics: (1) get_override_exclude_columns(this.name) drops rows matching override keys; (2) get_override_replace_columns(this.name) substitutes column values; (3) get_override_include_columns(...) UNIONs in extra rows. Override key columns are configured in dbt_project.yml var 'override_columns' = [ACCOUNT_ID, AGREEMENT_ID, AGREEMENT_LINE_ITEM_ID, OPPORTUNITY_ID, PRODUCT_CODE_L3, L4, L5, FISCAL_QUARTER_NAME].

Override sources are typically Google Sheets backed by Fivetran tables under BASE_PROD.GOOGLE_SHEETS.* (e.g. acv_override_created_date var for ACV corrections). The dbt_project.yml vars product_hierarchy_created_date and acv_override_created_date pin the override snapshot to a given Fivetran sync date.

Cross-project refs in eda-dbt-em use the dbt PROJECT NAME from the remote project's dbt_project.yml (not the GitHub repo name): {{ ref('eda_dbt_base', '<model>') }}, {{ ref('eda_dbt_gtm', '<model>') }}, {{ ref('eda_dbt_common', '<model>') }}, {{ ref('eda_dbt_cx', '<model>') }}. Names live in eda-dbt-em/dependencies.yml.

Available cross-project models: from eda_dbt_gtm -> wd_account_scd2 (joined in arr_line_categories for partner_name lookup), wd_proposal_line_scd2, wd_opportunity_daily_snapshot. From eda_dbt_base -> base_google_sheets_* (every Fivetran-synced sheet), base_salesforce_* (raw SF views), base_sox_* (SOX-compliant variants).

Model naming conventions in eda-dbt-em: stg_em_* (staging in eda-dbt-em, wraps source or cross-project ref), stg_em_int_* (intermediate stages that fan in multiple stg_em_*), stg_arr_categories_* (specific to ARR categories pipeline, all live under tmp_tbls_of_bt_arr_categories_optimized/), arr_*_categories (aggregate tables in FINANCE_PROD.AGGREGATIONS), arr_*_dashboard (views in FINANCE_PROD.DATA_PRODUCTS), wd_* (managed SCD1/SCD2 source-of-truth).

Snowflake-function vs dbt-model: get_*_fn lives in functions/managed/ and is invoked via select * from table({{ generate_function_db_schema_name() }}.get_*_fn(arg)). udf_* macros live in macros/em/snowflake_functions/ and emit SQL fragments inline. udf_tcv_to_arr, udf_is_preacquisition, udf_is_standalone_product_array, udf_product_mix_bb/eb/nn are the most frequently used.

build_line_id macro produces the synthetic line_id used as the grain key across arr_line_categories, stg_arr_categories_*, and get_arr_categories_fn. Always join on line_id + as_was_date + (optionally) fiscal_quarter_name to keep grain aligned.

Standard config for ARR aggregate tables: materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='delete+insert', unique_key='as_was_date', on_schema_change='append_new_columns', cluster_by=['as_was_date'], transient=false. unique_key='as_was_date' means a full as_was_date partition is deleted and re-inserted each run -- safe and idempotent.

Heavy aggregates set snowflake_warehouse=var('em_heavy_warehouse', none). When em_heavy_warehouse is set, dbt switches to that warehouse for the duration of the model. Use this for arr_product/subproduct/sku_categories. Leave None for staging/view models that fit on the default ANALYTICS_ENGINEER_WH.

Default as_was_date in dbt_project.yml is DATEADD(DAY,-1,CURRENT_DATE()) -- always D-1, never today. Override per run via --vars '{"as_was_date": "2026-02-11"}' for backfills or as-of-date analyses. Historical chain rebuilds use arr_refactor_as_was_date_list (4 dates: quarter-ends).

stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag is the FAN-IN: combines stg_em_int_financial_metrics (base) + stg_em_int_agree_base (account/partner lookup) + fix_partner_account_id BOW (Bill-of-Work) swap. Filters out 'NonMigrated-PBU-Manual' from agree_data_migrations. Used by finance_line_analytics as the primary input.

BOW (Bill of Work) account swap pattern: stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag swaps base.account_id for base.fix_account_id (the client) and base.partner_account_id for base.fix_partner_account_id. When account is swapped, ALL downstream account attributes (name, segment, region, industry) are also swapped via COALESCE. Important for partner-mediated deals where the contract is signed with the partner but ARR should attribute to the end-customer.

migration_category derivation in stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag: from opp_data_migrations LIKE '%PBU%' -> 'PBU', '%PKON%' -> 'Peakon', '%VNDLY%' -> 'VNDLY', NULL -> NULL, else 'TBD'. Used downstream to tag legacy migrated deals from acquired companies.

Fast-path / slow-path runtime selection in finance_line_analytics: uses Jinja adapter.get_columns_in_relation() to check if upstream stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag has the EDAEM-3704 columns (ENTITY_SOURCE, IS_ACQUIRED_SKU). If yes, skip the acquisition_flags join (saves a full scan of stg_em_int_agree_product_mapped). If no, fall back to filtered join. Pattern allows incremental rollout of schema changes without breaking existing pipelines.

Aggregate tables use WINDOW functions (sum(...) over (partition by ...)) instead of GROUP BY. Reason: preserves row-level columns alongside the aggregates so downstream views/queries can pick line-level OR aggregate-level values without re-joining. Standard pattern in arr_product/subproduct/sku_categories.

When summing splits / incrementals, ALWAYS partition by (account_id, opportunity_id, agreement_id, fiscal_quarter_name, product_code_l3, partner_account_id). Adding/removing a partition column shifts grain and produces wrong totals.

stg_arr_categories_* family (all in FINANCE_INT_PROD.STAGE) is the intermediate layer feeding arr_line_categories: stg_arr_categories_incremental (begin/end ARR + categories), stg_arr_categories_fiscal_attributes (FQ begin/end dates per line), stg_arr_categories_begin_balances + end_balances (per-FQ ARR balances), stg_arr_categories_fse_attributes (worker counts), stg_arr_categories_price_quantity (price/volume splits), stg_arr_categories_sku_swap (SKU migration mapping), stg_arr_categories_pending_renewals, stg_arr_categories_up_for_renewal, stg_arr_categories_related_lines, stg_arr_categories_sku_arr_event_type. All live under tmp_tbls_of_bt_arr_categories_optimized/.

SALES_PROD.MANAGED.WD_ACCOUNT is SCD1 (current state) -- 363 columns, joins 13+ base_salesforce_* tables (acc, user, recordtype) with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY _fivetran_synced DESC) = 1 to dedup latest. Produces derived fields: workday_type, employee_range_group (LE/ME), account_territory_label (concat_ws of all hierarchy levels), currency_conversion_rate. Use WD_ACCOUNT_SCD2 for historical / point-in-time lookups instead.

audit_columns_utc() macro is appended to every wd_* managed model in GTM. Emits columns like load_ts_utc / load_user / etc. for audit traceability. Don't filter these out when investigating data lineage.

ARR category helper macros (macros/em/arr_categories_helper.sql) generate the worker / FSE / price-quantity column expressions for all three tiers (sku/subproduct/product). fse_worker_columns(prefix, product_code_col) emits 17 worker MAX(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) expressions with a trailing comma (caller must NOT add a comma). pq_tier_aggregates(product_code_col, tier_prefix) emits the price/quantity SUM(...) OVER (...) expressions.

When writing macros that emit SQL inside SELECT lists, use {%- ... -%} and {{- ... -}} (with leading/trailing dashes) to strip whitespace and avoid extra spaces in compiled SQL. Pattern documented in arr_categories_helper.sql header comment.

udf_is_standalone_product_array('bb_product_mix') replaced the hardcoded SKU list in arr_product_categories. Now driven by master data in ref_product_hierarchy. New entity_source values in ref_product_hierarchy are picked up automatically without a code change. Same pattern should be used to refactor the hardcoded list in get_arr_categories_fn (currently still inline).

There is a parallel 'optimized' branch of the bt_*_arr_categories logic under models/finance/int/stage/table/tmp_tbls_of_bt_arr_categories_optimized/. This is the active code path (not legacy). The naming 'tmp_tbls_of_bt_*' is historical -- they are the canonical stages.

The eda-dbt-em qa-pinned bare clone lives at ~/Backups/eda-dbt-em-backup.git. Add a worktree with: git --git-dir=~/Backups/eda-dbt-em-backup.git worktree add --detach ~/Backups/eda-dbt-em-qa-mining qa. This is TCC-safe (outside ~/Documents/) so launchd background jobs can also read source.

When recursively mining source code, prefer reading the qa-pinned bare clone (~/Backups/eda-dbt-em-backup.git via worktree) over the user's main checkout. Reasons: (a) qa pin matches what is deployed; (b) doesn't disturb the user's branch state or uncommitted changes; (c) operates in TCC-safe location.

Slack users.lookupByEmail API returns 'not_allowed_token_type' for user-session tokens (lacks users:read.email scope). Fallback: use slackApi('search.messages', {query: 'from:@<handle>'}). The handle is typically the email prefix. Result includes user (Slack ID) and username fields. Validated 2026-06-25 with <person> and <person>.

FINANCE_PROD.AGGREGATIONS.ARR_LINE_CATEGORIES has 342 columns. Key positions: AS_WAS_DATE (1, DATE, cluster key), ACCOUNT_ID (2), AGREEMENT_ID (3), AGREEMENT_LINE_ITEM_ID (5), PRODUCT_CODE_L3 (22), L4 (24), L5 (26), LINE_ID (83), ARR_LINE_ID (84), OPP_COUNT (86), MISSING_ARR (87), FISCAL_QUARTER_NAME (88). The 3 main ARR category columns are at positions 141-143 (SKU/SUBPRODUCT/PRODUCT_ARR_CATEGORY). Avoid SELECT * -- query is 342 columns wide.

ARR effect decomposition columns in ARR_LINE_CATEGORIES (positions 317-329 for sku, 322-325 for subproduct, 327-329 for product): <tier>_CHANGE_ARR = total movement, decomposed into <tier>_VOLUME_ONLY_EFFECT_ARR + <tier>_PRICE_ONLY_EFFECT_ARR + <tier>_MIX_EFFECT_ARR. These four should sum to CHANGE_ARR within rounding. Used for price-volume-mix waterfall analyses.

ARR_LINE_CATEGORIES has 12 *_mix columns capturing the product mix at begin / end balance points: bb_sku_mix / bb_subproduct_mix / bb_product_mix (begin balance) + eb_*_mix (end balance) + begin_sku_mix / begin_subproduct_mix / begin_product_mix + end_*_mix. Use ARRAY_CONTAINS('<sku_code>'::variant, <mix_col>) for membership checks; never cast to string and use LIKE.

Product hierarchy levels in ARR tables: PRODUCT_CODE_L1 (top), L2, L3, L4, L5 (sku-level, leaf). Each has a matching PRODUCT_NAME_L*. Aggregations: arr_sku_categories rolls to L5, arr_subproduct_categories to L4, arr_product_categories to L3. There is no L6.

ARR Event-Type columns (positions 293-295, 315 in arr_line_categories): SKU/SUBPRODUCT/PRODUCT_ARR_EVENT_TYPE classifies the deal motion (New, Renewal, Amendment, etc.) and PRODUCT_ARR_RENEWAL_EVENT_TYPE adds the renewal-specific sub-classification. Derived in stg_arr_categories_sku_arr_event_type and joined back in arr_line_categories.

TCV -> ARR conversion formula (udf_tcv_to_arr macro, macros/em/udf_tcv_to_arr.sql): if DATEDIFF(day, start, end) > 0 then (value / (DATEDIFF(day,start,end) + 1)) * 365, else 0. Note the +1 on the denominator -- captures inclusive day count. Result cast to number(38,3). Always use this macro for TCV->ARR; do not hand-roll.

When agreement term is zero days or negative (data quality issue), udf_tcv_to_arr returns 0 (not NULL, not divide-by-zero). Audit queries should flag any line with TCV > 0 but ARR = 0 -- usually missing or inverted term dates.

GitHub uses ONLY ONE CODEOWNERS file per repo. Order of preference: `.github/CODEOWNERS` > `/CODEOWNERS` > `docs/CODEOWNERS`. If you add `.github/CODEOWNERS` it silently SHADOWS the root file's rules — happened in PR #408, reverted in PR #410. eda-dbt-em uses ROOT `/CODEOWNERS` as single source of truth (rules for *.sql → @workday-inc/eda-technical-lead, *.yml → eda-data-governance, .github/** → eda-devops). Never re-create `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

`@github-copilot` is NOT a valid CODEOWNERS handle — CODEOWNERS only resolves user/team handles, not GitHub Apps. Copilot reviewer is `copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]` and is invoked via repo / branch RULESETS, not CODEOWNERS. Wrong pattern (silently no-ops): `* @github-copilot`. Right pattern: enable a branch ruleset named e.g. `copilot_code_review` on qa, and Copilot picks up `.github/copilot-instructions.md` from the PR's base branch.

Snowflake FLOAT columns (binary floating-point) produce sub-cent rounding artifacts (e.g. -4.547e-13) that pass `!= 0` checks, causing adj_agreement_total_fees to incorrectly classify lines as 'Add On' instead of 'not categorized'. Fix from PR #330: replace every `adj_agreement_total_fees != 0` with `round(adj_agreement_total_fees, 2) != 0` in the UDF macro `snf_udf_get_arr_categories.sql` — 6 occurrences across min_term_start_in_fq_bysku / bysubproduct / byproduct CTEs.

Do NOT cast Snowflake FLOAT to INT directly when values are expected to evaluate to 1 — values like 0.4999 or 0.9999 get cast to 0 due to floating-point precision limits BEFORE type conversion. Fix from PR #309: `cast(round(<float_col>, 0) as int)` or `ceil(<float_col> - 0.5)`. Applied to quantity_change fields in get_price_quantity_fn.sql.

DO NOT use the `{{ function('...') }}` macro to call Snowflake UDFs — it does NOT resolve the database/schema path correctly across environments. Failed in PROD #412 with 'Unknown user-defined table function CERTIFIED_PROD.STAGE.GET_ARR_LINE_BASE_FN'. Use `{{ generate_function_db_schema_name() }}` instead — this is the canonical pattern used in stg_arr_categories_related_lines.sql and other models. Search the repo and replace every remaining `{{ function('...') }}` call.

VIEW vs TABLE deployment-order trap (PR #469): when you add a column to a VIEW (e.g. stg_em_int_agree_product_mapped) and a DOWNSTREAM table (e.g. stg_em_int_strategic_program_flag → finance_line_analytics) reads that column via the materialized table — the view deploys instantly but the table is rebuilt LATER in the dbt run. FLA referencing the new column will fail compile with 'invalid identifier' until the materialized table rebuild lands. Fix: source the new column directly from the BIRTH view (stg_em_int_agree_product_mapped) via an `acquisition_flags` CTE in the consumer, so column availability tracks view deploy not table-chain rebuild order.

When adding ADDITIVE flag columns (e.g. is_acquired_sku, is_pre_acquisition in EDAEM-3704/3707), source them from the BIRTH view (where the column is first defined) rather than threading them through every intermediate table in the chain. PR #469 added a small `acquisition_flags` CTE in FLA that joins directly to the stg_em_int_agree_product_mapped view on agreement_line_item_key and uses `qualify row_number()` to dedupe. Saves 80% of file diffs and dodges the view-vs-table deploy-order trap.
